metadata.title: Email SMTP and DNS
metadata.subject: NCC — Net-Centric Computing
metadata.contentType: Original practice based on the accompanying lecture notes

questions.question: Which DNS query normally locates mail exchangers for bob@recipient.example during direct relay?
options: A) An A query for bob
B) An MX query for recipient.example
C) An ARP query for recipient.example
D) A PTR query for the visible Subject field
questions.explanation: The recipient domain supplies MX records; a selected exchanger is then resolved to an IP address.

source.section: Section 5 — DNS and the destination mail server

questions.question: Two MX records have preferences 10 and 20. Which is preferred?
options: A) 20, because a larger value always means a faster server
B) Both must be contacted simultaneously for every recipient
C) The numbers determine TCP destination ports
D) 10, because lower preference values have higher priority
questions.explanation: MX preference is an ordering value, separate from port numbers and measured performance.

source.section: Section 5 — DNS and the destination mail server

questions.question: What does a null MX explicitly announce?
options: A) The domain has temporarily lost its DNS cache
B) The domain requires TCP port zero
C) The domain does not accept email
D) The domain accepts mail only through ARP
questions.explanation: An explicit null MX differs from a missing MX record and its possible fallback behavior.

source.section: Section 5 — DNS and the destination mail server

questions.question: What resolves an exchanger hostname into an address after MX lookup?
options: A) An A or AAAA lookup
B) Another SMTP DATA command
C) A TCP window scaling exchange
D) An Ethernet CRC lookup
questions.explanation: A provides IPv4 addresses and AAAA provides IPv6 addresses.

source.section: Section 5 — DNS and the destination mail server

questions.question: Which information normally controls the recipient delivery path in SMTP?
options: A) Only the visible To message header
B) The envelope RCPT TO recipients
C) The Ethernet source address
D) The Subject field
questions.explanation: Blind copies and forwarding demonstrate why envelope and visible headers can differ.

source.section: Section 4 — Email architecture and message structure

questions.question: Which server reply is the application acceptance point for transmitted message content?
options: A) A TCP ACK for the first content segment
B) A 250 reply to MAIL FROM before content
C) A successful final reply after the DATA content terminator
D) The server TCP SYN ACK
questions.explanation: The final SMTP success acknowledges acceptance at that server, separate from transport receipt.

questions.question: Why does a transmitted body line beginning with a dot have an extra leading dot?
options: A) SMTP uses dot transparency to distinguish content from its DATA terminator
B) TCP requires every line to begin with two bytes
C) DNS encodes all punctuation twice
D) Ethernet reserves the first dot for its checksum
questions.explanation: The receiver removes the extra leading dot when recovering content.

questions.question: What separates the Internet message header fields from the body?
options: A) The TCP SYN flag
B) The MX preference number
C) An Ethernet FCS
D) A blank line
questions.explanation: Message content has headers, a blank line, and a body.

source.section: Section 4 — Email architecture and message structure

questions.question: Which port normally serves server-to-server SMTP relay?
questions.explanation: Port 25 is the relay service; 587 and 465 are submission contexts and 53 is traditional DNS.

source.section: Section 4 — Email architecture and message structure

questions.question: What occurs after a successful STARTTLS negotiation?
options: A) The client switches the existing TCP connection to UDP
B) The receiver reuses the old capabilities without a new EHLO
C) The sender must resolve the recipient MAC across the Internet
D) A new EHLO is sent over TLS and earlier capability information is discarded
questions.explanation: STARTTLS resets relevant SMTP protocol knowledge after the TLS handshake.

questions.question: How does implicit TLS submission on port 465 begin?
options: A) SMTP DATA, then DNS, then the TLS handshake
B) An unencrypted SMTP greeting before any TLS handshake
C) A TLS handshake before an IP address is selected
D) TCP establishment, then TLS handshake, then SMTP greeting
questions.explanation: Implicit TLS starts protection immediately on the established TCP connection.

questions.question: What is the normal broad interpretation of an SMTP 451 reply?
options: A) A temporary failure that can lead to queued retry
B) Proof that the recipient has read the message
C) A successful content acceptance
D) A command to use IPv4 fragment offset 451
questions.explanation: A 4xx reply is a transient negative completion, distinct from 5xx permanent rejection.

questions.question: Which statement describes traditional DNS transport accurately?
options: A) It can use UDP or TCP, commonly with server port 53
B) It always uses the SMTP TCP connection
C) It uses ARP instead of transport
D) It cannot use TCP under any circumstances
questions.explanation: DNS is an independent application exchange and has TCP as well as UDP operation.

source.section: Section 5 — DNS and the destination mail server

questions.question: What does a TCP ACK of all message bytes prove?
options: A) The final SMTP content was accepted
B) The peer TCP has cumulatively received those stream bytes
C) The message is stored in the final mailbox
D) The message has been read by Bob
questions.explanation: Application acceptance is a separate protocol decision expressed by SMTP replies.

questions.question: Which service is normally responsible for Bob reading and synchronizing mailbox folders?
options: A) SMTP relay alone
B) IMAP
C) ARP
D) OSPF
questions.explanation: IMAP is mailbox access; SMTP handles message transfer.

source.section: Section 4 — Email architecture and message structure

questions.question: Why can a retry create a duplicate after the SMTP connection fails near the final reply?
options: A) TCP sequence numbers are reused for different recipients within one segment
B) Every SMTP error requires the recipient to create two mailboxes
C) The receiver may have accepted the content even though the client never received the final success
D) DNS always duplicates its MX records during retry
questions.explanation: The sender can be uncertain about application acceptance after a connection failure.
